related.reason_vi: Các cấu trúc dữ liệu thường dùng mà Java Collections Framework cài đặt thành các lớp cụ thể.

claims.evidence: Every explanation in the lesson was written from the class comments of the OpenJDK java.util sources at the pinned commit (Collection, Iterable, List, Set, Queue, Deque, Map, ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, TreeSet, PriorityQueue, ArrayDeque), read in raw copies; the inheritance relations were read from their declarations. The source article was used only for the names of the interfaces and classes. Documentation only; no behaviour was run.

claims.claim_vi: Collection is the root interface of the collection hierarchy; some collections allow duplicate elements and others do not, some are ordered and others are not; the JDK provides no direct implementations of Collection, only of more specific subinterfaces such as Set and List.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Collection extends Iterable; List (through SequencedCollection), Set and Queue extend Collection; Map does not extend Collection; Deque extends Queue.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Implementing Iterable allows an object to be the target of the enhanced for statement.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: List is an ordered collection where the user controls where each element is inserted and can access elements by integer index; lists typically allow duplicate elements; positional access may take time proportional to the index for some implementations such as LinkedList, so iterating is typically preferable to indexing when the implementation is unknown.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Set contains no pair of elements e1 and e2 such that e1.equals(e2); the behaviour of a set is not specified if an element is changed in a way that affects equals comparisons while it is in the set.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Queue is a collection designed for holding elements prior to processing; insert, remove and examine each exist in two forms (one throws an exception on failure, the other returns null or false); the special-value insert form is designed for capacity-restricted queues; queues typically, but not necessarily, order elements first-in-first-out, priority queues order by comparator or natural ordering, and every Queue implementation must specify its ordering.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Map maps keys to values; it cannot contain duplicate keys and each key maps to at most one value; it provides collection views of its keys (a Set), values (a Collection) and key-value mappings (a Set).
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: The Collection methods that add or remove elements are optional operations: an implementation that does not support one throws UnsupportedOperationException; List.of returns an unmodifiable list whose mutator methods always throw UnsupportedOperationException.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: ArrayList is a resizable-array List whose get and set run in constant time; LinkedList is a doubly-linked list implementing List and Deque whose indexed operations traverse from the nearer end; HashSet is backed by a hash table and does not guarantee iteration order; TreeSet orders elements by natural ordering or a Comparator given at creation.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: PriorityQueue orders elements by natural ordering or a Comparator and its head is the least element; ArrayDeque is a resizable-array Deque likely to be faster than LinkedList when used as a queue.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

design_notes_vi: Hình gồm phần gốc (Iterable, Collection), ba hợp đồng con kèm ví dụ lớp cài đặt, và nhắc Map nằm ngoài cây. Bỏ các tầng trung gian như SequencedCollection và Deque để thấy ba hợp đồng chính. Lời giải thích viết lại từ chú thích của mã nguồn JDK. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source text names no concrete classes (they appear only in its image); the lesson takes the class names from the source map and checks each against the OpenJDK sources.

The lesson does not follow the source's sequence of sentences: its explanations are written from the OpenJDK class comments (contracts of Collection, List, Set, Queue, Map and of the named classes), which the source does not contain.
Source does not say that Map is outside the Collection tree; the lesson adds it from the OpenJDK Map declaration.
Source does not mention optional operations, positional-access cost, changing set elements, or queue ordering; the lesson adds them from the OpenJDK class comments.
